title: Ingress Commit Coordinator: append-only buffer, probabilistic signature, and soft-typing reconciler
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Console produces high-volume usage events (console telemetry, API calls, billing ticks). Recent spikes exposed two correlated problems: duplicate events across retries/clients causing inflated metrics and tight schema validation rejecting real-world payload variance. Goal: introduce a resilient front-line coordinator that (1) provides an append-only commit buffer to absorb bursts and enable safe replay, (2) uses a lightweight probabilistic signature to catch cross-partition duplicates with low storage overhead, and (3) performs a delayed canonicalization pass that applies soft-typing/coercion rules before strict schema enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ingest pipeline accepts traffic under 2x baseline for 30 minutes without dropping; 2) Duplicate detection reduces observed duplicate rate by >= 80% in canary; 3) Schema rejection rate after canonicalization is <= 0.5% for canary customers; 4) Raw payloads preserved in commit buffer for at least 72 hours and reprocessable; 5) Feature gate toggles coordinator on/off without requiring client changes.
design_summary: Architecture: an append-only commit buffer (Kafka topic + commit index) accepts decrypted raw events from console backends. Each event is assigned a short probabilistic signature (64-bit rolling hash + Bloom fingerprint per tenant window) written alongside the raw message. The coordinator performs quick idempotency checks against an in-memory sliding window of recent signatures per shard to short-circuit obvious duplicates. Events then flow into a delayed canonicalizer that normalizes timestamp formats, coerces numeric-like strings to numbers where safe, trims long free-text fields, and attaches inferred attributes (region, route hash) used for routing and cost accounting. After canonicalization, events are validated against the schema service; failures are categorized as soft (coercible) or hard (structural mismatch). Soft failures enter a tolerant path with a transformation record; hard failures are flagged and routed to a quarantine stream with automatic retry/backoff and operator alerting.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Latency vs accuracy: delayed canonicalization adds processing time (~20-80ms) but dramatically reduces downstream rejections. We accept slightly higher tail latency in exchange for fewer customer-facing errors.
- False positives in probabilistic dedupe: Bloom-based signatures can drop unique events at a small rate; we budget false positive rate <= 1e-6 per tenant-day by tuning filter sizes.
- Storage overhead: commit buffer retention plus signatures increases storage costs; mitigated by 72h retention for raw with tiered archival to cheaper object storage after 72h.
- Operational complexity: introduces new metrics and recovery playbooks. Mitigation: clear runbooks, dashboards, and a shadow-mode rollout for 4 weeks before full traffic cutover.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow, 2 weeks): Coordinator runs in shadow for 100% traffic; metrics emitted but not acted on. Phase 1 (canary, 1% tenants, 48h): enable duplicate short-circuit and canonicalizer for selected tenants. Phase 2 (broaden, 25% tenants, 7 days): enable retry/quarantine path and monitor SLOs. Phase 3 (full): enable coordinator globally and retire a legacy prefilter. Each phase guarded by kill-switch feature flag; automatic rollback on SLA regression (>2x error rate or >1% increase in p95 latency).
metrics_and_alerts: Track: commit_buffer_write_lag_ms, commit_buffer_retention_bytes, dedupe_detected_rate, dedupe_false_positive_estimate, canonicalization_time_p50_p95, schema_reject_rate_post_canonicalization, quarantined_events_per_min, reprocess_success_rate. Alerts: any sustained schema_reject_rate_post_canonicalization > 1% for 10m, dedupe_false_positive_estimate spike, commit_buffer_write_lag > 500ms.
migration_and_rollforward:
- Instrument an export job to sample 1% of historical raw payloads and run them through canonicalizer to adjust coercion rules.
- Provide a backfill reprocessor that reads commit buffer from a specified offset and replays into the pipeline after rules update.
- Add a tenant scoped 'strict' flag to preserve pre-canonicalization behavior for customers that require exact receipts.
testing_plan: Unit tests for probabilistic signature generator and Bloom filter boundaries. Integration test that injects controlled duplicate and malformed payloads to verify end-to-end paths (short-circuit, canonicalize+accept, quarantine+retry). Load test with 2x QPS for 1 hour in a staging environment. Chaos test: simulate commit buffer node loss and validate re-replication and reprocessing.
